---
title: "Performance"
---

phplyr's functions call one or two methods of the table they are given, so
the backend determines how fast a pipeline runs. These timings cover the
workloads and machine below.

## Methods

Every record comes from one Linux machine: two pinned AMD Zen 5 cores
(Ryzen 9 9955HX), 8 GB of memory, Ubuntu 24.04, and PHP 8.5.12, with phibble
0.6.0 and phpolars 0.2.1 (Polars 0.55.2 at two threads). DataFrame and SQLite
run single-threaded. Each timing is the median of seven runs, and each record
lists every run.

| Script | Measures | Timer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bench/harness.php` | phibble's shared workloads on DataFrame, SQLite, and PolarsTable, each as a phplyr pipeline and as direct table calls | Through `collect()`; loading the data is not timed |
| `bench/backends.php` | Three pipelines on DataFrame, PolarsTable, and SQLite, checking that all return the same rows | Through `collect()`; loading the data is not timed |
| `bench/backends.R` | Two of those pipelines with dplyr 1.2.1 on R 4.6.2, checking row counts and column sums against phplyr's | On a preloaded tibble |
| `bench/models.php` | `lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and `glmer()` on the phit extension and phit-polyfill | One fit per fresh process, after the data is generated |

The harness data comes from `bench/generate.php`, with phibble's generator
and seed. `events.csv` has 1,000,000 rows of `id`, `key` (10,000 values), `g`
(8 labels), `x` (float, about 2% NA), and `t` (datetime). `dims.csv` has
100,000 rows of `key`, `label`, and `w`.

## phplyr's overhead

The median phplyr pipeline and the median direct table calls differed by at
most 3%, with two exceptions. The 15 ms PolarsTable summary differed by
1.2 ms. The closure filters varied by up to 40% from run to run in both
forms.

## phibble workloads at 1,000,000 rows

| Workload | DataFrame (s) | SQLite (s) | PolarsTable (s) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| Grouped `summarise()` of `n()`, `mean()`, and `sum()` by `key` | 0.15 | 0.50 | 0.015 |
| The same with closures | 0.46 | 2.10 | 0.79 |
| Grouped `arrange(t)`, then `mutate()` with `lag()`, `cumsum()`, and `row_number()` | 1.03 | 5.16 | 0.49 |
| `filter(col('x')->gt(0)->and(...))` | 0.16 | 0.34 | 0.05 |
| The same filter as a closure | 1.11 | 2.78 | 1.55 |
| `mutate()` with two expressions | 0.27 | 2.47 | 0.53 |
| `left_join()` of 1M × 100k rows on `key` | 0.34 | 3.31 | 0.61 |
| `arrange(desc('x'), 'id')` | 0.87 | 2.56 | 0.56 |

The records are
[`harness-dataframe.json`](benchmarks/harness-dataframe.json),
[`harness-sqlite.json`](benchmarks/harness-sqlite.json), and
[`harness-polars.json`](benchmarks/harness-polars.json).

## Choosing a backend

- **In-memory `DataFrame`** suits data that fits in memory. In the grouped
  summary above, expression arguments took 0.15 s and closures 0.46 s,
  because phibble computes expressions in one pass without building a table
  per group.
- **A database table (`Phibble\tbl()`)** avoids loading the data into PHP.
  With expressions, `filter()` and `summarise()` run in the database, and only
  the result reaches PHP.
- **Pipelines that return every row** (`mutate()`, `arrange()`, unfiltered
  joins) spend most of their database time transferring rows to PHP.
- **Closures on a database table** load all rows first and then run in
  memory. Use `col()` expressions and phplyr's helpers to keep the work in
  SQL.
- **SQLite columns need declared types.** PDO binds values as strings. In an
  untyped column, SQLite stores them as text and compares numbers as text.
- **PolarsTable** (phibble's Polars backend, on the phpolars extension) runs
  expressions in Polars and converts the result to PHP values. Every
  expression workload above was faster than on DataFrame except the
  `mutate()` and the join, which return all 1M rows after little
  computation.
- **Closure steps on PolarsTable** convert the data to a DataFrame and back,
  so both closure workloads above were slower on PolarsTable than on
  DataFrame.
- **Data that starts in Polars** can skip phibble's CSV parse with
  `PolarsTable::fromPolars(Phpolars\read_csv($path))`.

## Backend pipelines

`bench/backends.php` checks that every backend returns the same rows, and
`bench/backends.R` checks dplyr's row counts and column sums against
phplyr's.

- **A:** filter, join a store lookup, two-key summarise, then a ranking window.
- **B:** grouped `lag(orderBy:)`, `cumsum()`, and a share of the group total
  over all rows.
- **C:** pipeline A with a closure in `filter()`. It has no dplyr version,
  because its closure is PHP code.

The input is a generated `sales` table, with no date or datetime columns,
joined to a 100-row `stores` table.

| Pipeline, 1M rows | DataFrame (s) | PolarsTable (s) | SQLite (s) | dplyr (s) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| A: reduce to a ranked summary | 0.71 | 0.10 | 0.59 | 0.12 |
| B: windows over every row | 1.85 | 0.52 | 4.01 | 0.03 |
| C: A with a closure | 1.28 | 1.19 | 2.24 | |

The records, with the 100,000-row results, are
[`backends-results.json`](benchmarks/backends-results.json) and
[`dplyr-results.json`](benchmarks/dplyr-results.json).
